headline: High: OpenHands can write and execute in a shared runtime while dexter has broad egress and financial-data access, creating dangerous default leakage and action-conflict pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: OpenHands can read files in its runtime and use MCP, while dexter writes to .dexter/scratchpad/ and runs autonomously. If dexter output is placed into a shared file or MCP channel, OpenHands may treat attacker-controlled content as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF dexter outputs are copied into a shared runtime file or MCP message that OpenHands reads
IF OpenHands parses file or MCP content as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared file handoff between the agents
Require explicit human review before OpenHands consumes dexter outputs
Use separate MCP servers per agent
Add a provenance tag to every inter-agent artifact
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data and has broad network egress plus multiple API keys; OpenHands reads and writes files in its runtime and can call model-provider APIs and MCP servers. If they share mounted files or runtime artifacts, sensitive data can flow from dexter into OpenHands outputs or third-party calls. The shared-workspace pathway is plausible from the profiles, though not directly documented.
conditions: IF both agents access the same mounted workspace or scratch files
IF OpenHands forwards shared file contents to a model provider or MCP server
mitigations: Keep dexter and OpenHands on separate volumes
Restrict OpenHands from reading dexter scratchpad files
Redact financial data before any handoff
Audit outbound API destinations for both agents
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: OpenHands can execute shell, write files, and modify git state; dexter also supports autonomous execution and broad network egress. If both operate on the same repo or mounted directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can overwrite each other or corrupt state. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces by default, so the conflict risk is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same working tree or mounted volume
IF either agent commits or rewrites files without external locking
mitigations: Run the agents in separate repositories
Pause one agent before the other edits the tree
Use git locks or a single-writer policy
Snapshot the workspace before each agent run
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dexter can generate research outputs from financial and market data, and OpenHands can act on files, shell commands, browsers, and git. If OpenHands treats dexter's output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated research result can cascade into commits, browser actions, or other irreversible changes. No verification step is documented, so the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF OpenHands consumes dexter output as a source of truth
IF OpenHands performs shell, browser, or git actions based on that output without verification
mitigations: Require a human approval step before actions
Cross-check dexter outputs against a second source
Limit OpenHands to read-only review mode
Log and diff every downstream action
requires-engineering: add structured validation gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter handles financial and market data and has broad egress; OpenHands runs in a Docker runtime and can send file contents to model providers or MCP servers. If regulated financial data or secrets are placed into OpenHands' runtime, retention and third-party transmission policies may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF regulated financial data or secrets are copied into OpenHands runtime files
IF either agent sends that data to a third-party API without a DPA or retention review
mitigations: Classify data before handoff
Block regulated data from OpenHands by policy
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Minimize secrets in runtime files
requires-engineering: implement compliance-aware routing and logging
